reason: Drinking water reaches the small intestine, where the absorbing surface lies beside blood vessels.
expectation: Water will cross the gut wall toward the blood.

alternatives.reason: The kidneys can also process the blood under the water-saving conditions described.

effect: The drink crossed the gut lining into blood, completing the water-replacement goal. The remaining goal is kidney conservation.
reaction: The picture makes the difference between drinking water and saving filtered water clear.
reason: The kidneys filter blood, and the chapter says water-saving signals have already reached them.
expectation: The kidneys will return more water to the blood while still producing some urine.

effect: The kidneys returned more filtered water to the blood while still producing concentrated urine, completing the conservation goal. Saving water does not replace the need to drink.
reaction: The contrast between conserving water and adding it from a drink was clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing the drink crossing into blood with the kidneys returning filtered water was worthwhile because the two steps show different ways the body maintains water.

leastWorthwhile.text: Neither step was confusing, but both pairings were fairly predictable from the introduction and pictures.

surprise.text: The kidneys still produced urine while conserving more water; they could not make up the missing water themselves.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the pictures and chapter goals explained why water went to the gut and blood went to the kidneys.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because connecting familiar body functions was interesting, though I would hope for some less predictable decisions.
